EMPIRICAL RESEARCH PLAN  

================================================================  
1. Identification Strategy  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
Method: Difference-in-Differences (two-way fixed effects) complemented with a dynamic event-study.  

Why DID is appropriate  
• The policy shock (1990-1994 tariff cuts) is common in calendar time but heterogeneous in intensity across municipalities because of their pre-reform industrial mix.  
• We observe repeated cross-sections/panel of municipalities before and after the reform, allowing us to compare changes in outcomes in high- versus low-exposure areas.  
• The reform was announced and implemented rapidly, limiting anticipatory behaviour.  
• A dynamic event-study around the liberalisation years provides a transparent pre-trend test and allows effect heterogeneity over time.  

Extension (optional but recommended): Use a shift-share instrument—predicted municipal tariff reduction based on 1989 employment shares × national tariff schedule—to instrument for actual tariff cuts. This absorbs any endogenous local lobbying that could have affected realised tariffs.  

================================================================  
2. Treatment and Control  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
Treatment variable  
TariffCut_i = Σ_s (EmpShare_is,1989 × ΔTariff_s,90-94)  
where s indexes 4-digit industries, EmpShare_is,1989 is the share of municipal employment in industry s in 1989, and ΔTariff_s,90-94 is the percentage-point reduction in the MFN tariff in that industry between 1990 and 1994. It is a continuous “dose” measure (larger value ⇒ larger exposure).  

Binary treatment (for descriptive graphs only)  
Treated = 1{TariffCut_i ≥ median} ; Control = 1{TariffCut_i < median}.  

Control group / Counterfactual  
Municipalities in the lowest quartile (or below the median) of TariffCut_i serve as the main counterfactual. Results will be shown both with the continuous dose and with this binary split to ease interpretation.  

Treatment timing  
Post_t = 1 for years 1994 and onward (first full year after the main tranche of cuts). Pre_t = 0 for 1986-1990. Years 1991-1993 are “transition” and will be kept but flagged in the event study.  

(If the IV extension is used) Instrument  
PredTariffCut_i = Σ_s (EmpShare_is,1985 × ΔTariff_s,national,90-94) where pre-reform national tariff schedule is interacted with historic municipal employment shares.  

================================================================  
3. Key Identifying Assumptions  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
A1. Parallel Trends: In the absence of the reform, municipalities with different TariffCut_i would have evolved similarly.  
Plausibility: Industrial composition in 1989 was shaped by a long period of import-substitution policy, arguably unrelated to the rapid liberalisation that followed. Event-study pre-coefficients will test this.  

A2. No Anticipation / Timing Accuracy: Economic agents did not change behaviour before the reform in ways correlated with TariffCut_i.  
Plausibility: The Collor Plan and subsequent tariff decrees were announced and executed over a short horizon (1990-1992).  

A3. Stable Composition (SUTVA): Outcomes in one municipality are not directly affected by tariff cuts in another (no spillovers).  
Plausibility: Migration across municipalities is non-trivial in Brazil, so this is the weakest assumption; will be probed by excluding large metro areas and by looking at net-migration as an outcome.  

(If IV is used)  
A4. Relevance: PredTariffCut_i strongly predicts actual tariff exposure.  
A5. Exclusion: PredTariffCut_i affects outcomes only through actual tariff changes, conditional on controls and fixed effects.  

================================================================  
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigation  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
T1. Differential pre-trends in declining manufacturing regions.  
• Mitigation: Show event-study pre-period coefficients; include state-year fixed effects; control for 1980-1985 growth rates interacted with year dummies.  

T2. Concurrent macro reforms (Real Plan 1994, privatizations) correlated with industrial mix.  
• Mitigation: Add state-year or region-sector-year fixed effects; control for privatization exposure; re-estimate excluding post-1994 years to focus on 1990-1993.  

T3. Labour mobility / spillovers.  
• Mitigation: (i) Estimate effects on population as a separate outcome; (ii) re-run regressions using “commuting zones” or meso-regions so that treatment variation is less prone to migration; (iii) cluster SEs at the micro-region level.  

================================================================  
5. R Code Outline  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
```r
# Load libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(fixest)      # fast TWFE and IV
library(modelsummary)

# 1. Data loading ---------------------------------------------------------
muni <- read_csv("municipality_outcomes.csv")        # outcome data: wages, employment
tariff <- read_csv("industry_tariff_changes.csv")    # Δ tariff by industry
empl   <- read_csv("employment_shares_1989.csv")     # 1989 employment shares

# 2. Construct tariff-cut exposure ---------------------------------------
# Merge tariff changes into employment shares
tariff_exp <- empl %>% 
  left_join(tariff, by = "industry4") %>%
  mutate(weighted_cut = emp_share_1989 * delta_tariff) %>%
  group_by(municipality_id) %>%
  summarise(tariff_cut = sum(weighted_cut, na.rm = TRUE))

# Predicted instrument using 1985 shares (if available)
empl85 <- read_csv("employment_shares_1985.csv")
pred_exp <- empl85 %>% 
  left_join(tariff, by = "industry4") %>%
  mutate(weighted_cut = emp_share_1985 * delta_tariff) %>%
  group_by(municipality_id) %>%
  summarise(pred_tariff_cut = sum(weighted_cut, na.rm = TRUE))

# Combine with outcomes
panel <- muni %>%
  left_join(tariff_exp, by = "municipality_id") %>%
  left_join(pred_exp,  by = "municipality_id") %>%
  mutate(post = if_else(year >= 1994, 1, 0),
         treat_intensity = post * tariff_cut)

# 3. Main TWFE regression -------------------------------------------------
# Employment as outcome
twfe_main <- feols(emp_rate ~ post*tariff_cut + 
                     control_vars | municipality_id + year, 
                   data = panel, 
                   cluster = ~state_id)

etable(twfe_main, se = "cluster")

# 4. Dynamic event-study --------------------------------------------------
ev <- feols(emp_rate ~ sunab(year, tariff_cut) + control_vars | 
              municipality_id + year, 
            data = panel, cluster = ~state_id)

iplot(ev, ref.line = 1990)   # pre-trends visualization

# 5. IV specification (optional) -----------------------------------------
iv_main <- feols(emp_rate ~ post*tariff_cut | post*pred_tariff_cut + 
                   control_vars | municipality_id + year,
                 data = panel, cluster = ~state_id)
etable(twfe_main, iv_main, se = "cluster")

# 6. Robustness: placebo test using 1984-1989 only ------------------------
placebo <- feols(emp_rate ~ lead(post, 4)*tariff_cut | 
                   municipality_id + year,
                 data = filter(panel, year <= 1989),
                 cluster = ~state_id)
etable(placebo, se = "cluster")
```
Notes  
• `control_vars` = vector of time-varying covariates (log population, education share, etc.).  
• SEs clustered at state or meso-region level to allow spatial correlation.  

================================================================  
6. Expected Results  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
Theory predicts import-competing locations should see employment and wage declines when tariffs fall. Prior evidence (e.g., U.S.–China shock) suggests a −2 % to −6 % employment effect per 10 pp larger tariff cut over 5-10 years. I expect a −3 % employment effect and −1.5 % wage effect per 10 pp cut within five years.  

================================================================  
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
(1 = clearly satisfied, 0 = questionable/absent)  

C1: Parallel pre-trend visually/ statistically verified ….………… 1  
C2: No major concurrent shocks correlated with treatment …… 0.5  
C3: Correct timing / limited anticipation …………………………… 1  
C4: Stable composition / limited spillovers …………………… 0.5  
C5: Robustness across alternative specs upheld ……………… 1  

TOTAL = 4/5. With the IV extension and migration robustness, C2-C4 would likely improve.
